workflow: Map the original clothing asset, LOD and skeletal mesh sections. Verify the converted cloth asset binds to the intended sections.
Identify the host asset and terminal node. Follow the typed connections upstream to locate the requested simulation or deformation stage.
Capture the existing graph as text and the affected pin types. Make the smallest graph edit, then read back node links and defaults.
Identify the existing sun, sky light, atmosphere and fog actors in the level. Adjust the component that controls the requested effect and compare the same camera view.
Search for an existing material and inspect its exposed parameters. Use a material instance for parameter-only changes and verify its parent and overrides.
Look up related project skills first. Give a new skill a distinct trigger, keep its workflow specific to the task and retrieve it again after registration.
Choose a component or a spawned effect according to ownership and lifetime. Match user parameter names and types on the system before wiring Blueprint values.
Inventory modules, parameter reads and renderer bindings. Report orphan candidates with their consumers before acting on a cleanup request.
Identify the dynamic input's output type and simulation target. Use an expression that yields that type and check the equivalent behavior on the intended target.
Inspect a comparable emitter template, its simulation target and its stack stages. Place parameter writes before the stage and renderer that consume them.
Match a system template to the effect and how it starts. Check orientation, attachment, looping and scale on the level instance.
Measure the expensive emitters on the target platform. Isolate simulation, renderer and bounds costs before tuning one budget and comparing again.
Choose the renderer from the effect's geometry and lifetime. Verify the material usage and the particle attributes consumed by its bindings.
Identify the selection or spline and preview the PCG operation footprint. Verify the batch result and keep a way to undo unintended placements.
Curate the assets to compare and choose a clear placement area. Arrange the lineup with consistent spacing and check each item is represented.
Identify the biome definition, generator, filters and contributing level actors. Trace how a sampled point acquires its biome and chosen asset.
Follow a failing sample through point generation, biome assignment, filtering and spawning. Locate the first stage where valid points disappear.
Inspect an example graph, available node types and graph inputs. Trace data and attributes through the requested edit and inspect representative output.
Identify the source mesh actor and sampling graph. Check local transforms, surface orientation and instance density on a representative mesh.
Inspect the mesh partition, tile bounds and priority inputs. Read a representative terrain region before applying a spatially scoped change.
Resolve the spline, grammar rules and module sizes. Check the expansion for a representative segment, including leftover length.
